newsitem.title: USA: Boston Fed's Minehan sees limited price pressures.
newsitem.headline: Boston Fed's Minehan sees limited price pressures.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Cathy Minehan on Monday cited only limited signs of price pressures in the otherwise healthy U.S. economy.

"Throughout this period of strong employment and output performance, the core rate of inflation remained remarkably well-behaved," Minehan told the annual conference of the Association of Business Economists.

"Surges in oil and grain prices contributed to a small increase in overall consumer price inflation. But it appears that these industry-specific price disruptions may not feed into overall wages and prices," Minehan addd.
Minehan, echoing a theme previously stated by other Fed officials, stressed such scattered price pressures "could thus amount to only temporary disruptions in the longer-run trajectory of inflation."
Minehan also predicted "higher (market) interest rates may keep these spending categories from growing and may make a relatively high level of consumer debt more burdensome."
The Fed's forecast for an economic slowdown, now expected to be most felt in the fourth quarter, is based, in part, on the impact of higher Treasury yields on rate-sensitive sectors of the economy.
Minehan also cautioned "the business cycle is hardly dead," in reference to the series of boom-bust periods the U.S. economy has experienced since World War II.
Turning to productivity, Minehan said technology changes are "raising concerns about how fast we can grow and whether the benefits of such growth will be shared by all."

Minehan noted the impact of technology on the economy -- or the "component of economic growth that cannot be accounted for by changes in the stocks of capital and labor in the economy" -- "remains something of a mystery."
Fed officials have said the combination of healthy growth and low inflation enjoyed by the services-heavy U.S. economy may result from technology changes whose impact is difficult to estimate.
